study.title: Imaging the functional connectivity of the Periaqueductal Gray during genuine and sham electroacupuncture treatment
study.study_design: Randomized placebo-controlled study with 2x2 factorial design (treatment mode x expectancy level); new analysis of previously collected fMRI dataset
study.randomization: Subjects were randomized to one of four groups: genuine EA or sham EA paired with either high expectancy (HE) or low expectancy (LE) manipulation
study.blinding: Not explicitly described for participants beyond sham needle use; acupuncture-naive subjects; blinding success not formally assessed in this paper
study.population: Seventy-seven healthy, right-handed subjects; all subjects were acupuncture naive and had no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders
study.inclusion_criteria: Healthy, right-handed, acupuncture naive, no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders
study.exclusion_criteria: History of neurological or psychiatric disorders

extraction_notes.note: Table 1 for sham EA state has incomplete coordinate triplets for several rows. The columns for x, y, z are not clearly separated for rows: Right frontal operculum/inferior frontal gyrus (appears as '45 21 15' but table structure is ambiguous), Right anterior insula/inferior frontal gyrus (appears as '42 27 3'), Left postcentral gyrus/inferior parietal lobule (appears as '63 -24 42'), Right inferior parietal lobule (appears as '-66 -33 33'), and Bilateral ACC/MPFC, MCC (appears as '0 35 27'). It is unclear from the PDF rendering whether these are complete coordinate triplets or partial. All three values were recorded as-is based on the text that could be parsed.

For Table 1 sham EA state rows, cluster sizes for Right frontal operculum/inferior frontal gyrus, Right anterior insula/inferior frontal gyrus, and Bilateral ACC/MPFC MCC are not clearly visible in the PDF rendering. The cluster size column appears cut off or not present for those rows.
Adverse events are not mentioned in the paper. The paper does not report whether any adverse events occurred during acupuncture or sham acupuncture administration.

Individual MASS subscale mean and SD values are not provided in the paper. Only narrative comparisons (higher/lower/similar) between groups are reported for individual subscales. Overall ANOVA F statistic and p value are provided.
Trial registration number is not reported anywhere in the paper.

Blinding success or allocation guessing was not formally assessed in this paper. The authors note subjects were acupuncture naive and were un-blinded after participation, but no blinding check instrument is reported.

The paper refers to this as a 'new analysis of previously unpublished data collected in a randomized placebo-controlled study [29,30].' The primary clinical and pain rating results are reported separately in references [29] and [30]. This paper focuses only on the fcMRI analysis during the EA stimulation scan. Clinical behavioral outcomes beyond MASS ratings are not provided here.

The n_analyzed for individual contrasts is inferred: for contrasts pooling all 4 groups (main effects) n=48; for 2-group post-hoc comparisons n=24 (12 per group). The paper does not explicitly state per-contrast sample sizes; these are derived from reported group sizes.

The paper notes a scanner upgrade mid-study from Siemens Allegra to Siemens TIM Trio, with 6-8 subjects per group on old scanner and 4-6 subjects per group on new scanner. The scanner type was not included as a covariate in the reported fcMRI analyses; however, the authors describe careful randomization and acquisition parameter matching.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods/fMRI Data Acquisition and Analysis section, page 3

extraction_notes.note: Table 2 note states threshold was 'voxel-wise p < 0.001 uncorrected with 20 continuous voxels,' which differs from the main methods text and Table 1 note which specify 31 contiguous voxels. This discrepancy is preserved as reported.

extraction_notes.note: The seed location (MNI 0 -28 -10) is described as from a 'previous analysis' in reference [30]. This is not independently derived in this paper; it is adopted from the prior publication. The paper describes this as the ventral PAG belonging to the 'analgesic zone.'

The paper does not specify which software was used for preprocessing or primary functional connectivity analysis beyond mentioning AlphaSim for cluster correction. No SPM, FSL, AFNI, or other software version is named for the main pipeline.

The expectancy manipulation for HE groups involved covertly decreasing thermal stimuli temperatures in Session 2 to create an unmistakable experience of analgesia, while LE groups received no such manipulation. In Session 3, HE subjects received only one reduced-temperature stimulus as an 'expectancy boost.' This complex manipulation may confound neural results between expectancy groups, as acknowledged by the authors.

For the sham EA group, the functional connectivity scan analysis used the same epoch-splitting approach (3 epochs of 6 minutes corresponding to the current-ON periods for genuine EA). For sham EA subjects, there was no actual current; the epoch timing was matched. The paper states 'in which the current was turned on for participants receiving genuine EA' but does not explicitly clarify how sham epochs were defined for the fcMRI analysis.

The arm_id assignments for conditions and contrasts in the sham group use 'arm_sham_HE' as representative. In fact, sham EA comprised both HE and LE groups. Where conditions or contrasts pool both sham groups, arm_id is approximate. The paper pools both sham groups for the main effect of acupuncture mode analysis.
